C005.subject: AI systems with explicit causal structure learning modules that incorporate thermodynamic free-energy minimization
C005.object: linear scaling with task complexity measured by number of latent confounders, but only up to a threshold of 7 confounders, beyond which scaling becomes exponential due to entropic bottlenecks in the causal graph search
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AI systems with explicit causal structure learning modules that incorporate thermodynamic free-energy minimization linear scaling with task complexity measured by number of latent confounders, but only up to a threshold of 7 confounders, beyond which scaling becomes exponential due to entropic bottlenecks in the causal graph search]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled simulation experiments systematically varying the number of latent confounders from 1 to 12 in a causal Bayesian network structure learning task using a thermodynamic free-energy minimization algorithm (e.g., a variant of Boltzmann machine or variational annealing). — Directly tests the predicted linear-to-exponential transition at 7 confounders, measuring computational cost (e.g., FLOPs or iterations) vs. confounder count under idealized single-threaded conditions. Replication across multiple random graph topologies would confirm or refute the threshold and scaling form.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the entropic bottleneck in causal graph search: derive scaling laws for the partition function or free-energy landscape complexity as a function of latent variable count in low-complexity inference tasks. — Provides a formal mathematical foundation for the hypothesized threshold. If analysis shows that the entropy of the posterior over graphs grows exponentially beyond a critical number of confounders (e.g., due to combinatorial explosion in latent variable assignments), it would support the hypothesis; if it shows polynomial growth, it would refute the exponential scaling claim.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of prior work on thermodynamic AI and causal structure learning, focusing on scaling behavior with latent variables, such as studies on free-energy-based structure learning in restricted Boltzmann machines or variational autoencoders. — Identifies existing empirical or theoretical results that may already confirm or contradict the predicted threshold. For instance, papers on 'thermodynamic computing' or 'causal discovery with latent confounders' might reveal similar scaling patterns or alternative bottlenecks, providing indirect evidence without new simulations.

scope.domain: low-complexity causal inference tasks with limited computational budgets

qualifier.temporal: simulated under idealized single-threaded conditions as of 2025
